match.reason: No point in the bank covers net foreign debt, foreign equity or net foreign liabilities; the balance of payments point deals only with current account flows, not the stock of foreign liabilities.

draft.title: Foreign debt and foreign equity
card: money Australians owe to lenders overseas, such as a bank borrowing from a foreign bank. It must be repaid, with interest.
ownership of Australian assets by foreigners, such as shares in a company or a stake in a mine. It is not repaid. Owners receive a share of profits, called dividends.
Net foreign debt is what Australians owe overseas lenders, minus what Australians are owed by borrowers overseas. Net foreign equity works the same way for ownership.
Net foreign liabilities = net foreign debt + net foreign equity. This is the total amount owed or owned by the rest of the world, after taking away Australian claims overseas.
draft.remember: Debt is owed back to lenders. Equity is ownership. Add them to get net foreign liabilities.

a.q: A Japanese company buys shares in an Australian mining firm. What does this add to?
opts: Foreign equity
Foreign debt
Net foreign debt only
Australia's overseas assets
a.why: Buying shares gives the Japanese company part ownership of an Australian firm. That is foreign equity. It is not debt, because nothing is lent and there is no loan to repay.
a.clue: Did the buyer lend money or take ownership?

b.q: An Australian bank borrows $2 billion from a bank in London. Later, a Singapore fund buys a 20% stake in an Australian airport. What happens to net foreign liabilities?
opts: Both add to them, the loan as debt, the stake as equity
Only the loan adds to them, as it is a debt
Only the stake adds to them, as it is ownership
Neither adds to them until the loan is repaid
b.why: The loan adds to net foreign debt and the stake adds to net foreign equity. Net foreign liabilities is the total of both, so both raise it. Equity is not debt, but it still counts as a liability to the rest of the world.
b.clue: Net foreign liabilities include both debt and equity.

b.best: Both add to them, the loan as debt, the stake as equity

problems.detail: The clue 'Net foreign liabilities include both debt and equity' gives the answer away. A student can pick 'Both add to them' without working through either transaction.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. The only problem is that the clue for question b states the answer outright and should be reworded so students must still reason it out.
